analysis: The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md (new shape-warmup section at head lines ~716-749, with the visible units being unchanged surrounding text) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (head line 1687, a new env var row for DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SHAPE_WARMUP). No executable code, wire protocol, authorization, attestation, key handling or cache-storage behavior is changed in the supplied evidence. The documented warmup runs greedy probes and shape cells at model load, excluded from calibration counters, under a 20 s wall budget. Per the doc it does not train rates and runs before registration or listener open, so it does not add a consumer-facing surface. The new env var only disables the warmup (`0`) or skips its shader-cache probe (`always`). It is a local operator control and, from the docs, affects only latency and availability, not confidentiality. Warmup prompts use synthetic probes; I could not verify from the supplied text that they are content-free or that they never touch the SSD prefix cache. If the implementation donated warmup prefixes to the encrypted SSD cache (T-041), that would be a cache-pollution/timing concern. The source for ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup was not supplied. The 750 ms timing thresholds are not tied to a security decision. Residual questions for any code-bearing review of this PR: (1) whether warmup requests bypass prefix-cache donation and the coordinator cacheSalt scoping; (2) whether they are admitted through the KV budget and process ledger so they cannot starve live requests; (3) whether the preload ordering before registration holds when the warmup times out. No finding is raised on documentation alone.
